name: In-silico task readiness and adaptive waiting on the authors' B3 model
context: Simulation on one published model structure (B3, the authors' 1000 posterior samples); results describe that model, not measured cells, and are never reported as experimental benefits.

Posterior samples express population-mean uncertainty, not cell heterogeneity. Controllers use the other 999 samples (leave-one-out), so they share the plant's structure: an optimistic setting without structural mismatch.
Doses, durations and waits follow the candidate design of validation_kit/configs/validation_registration_draft.json. No readiness or policy outcome had been simulated when this protocol was frozen.
history_note: The previous command ends at time 0; the probe is applied after a wait w.

task.response: incremental rise: maximum noise-free FRET over [w, w+20] minus FRET at w (1-min grid)
task.success: rise >= 0.8 x the same sample's rise to a 5-min probe on an unstimulated receiver
task.completion_min: w + 20 for success; deadline D = 140 for failure (failure-penalized completion time)

observations: Plant FRET of the history-only trajectory at decision times 0, 2, ..., 120 min plus Gaussian noise sd 0.005 (seed 20261005 + plant index), available at the decision time.

policies.fixed_wait: probe at w in {6, 12, 24, 48} (registered candidates); the full fixed-wait curve over the grid is also reported.
policies.threshold_reset: probe at the first decision time with observed FRET <= 1.01, otherwise at 120.
policies.readiness_current: probe at the first decision time where the estimated success probability >= 0.9, estimated from the current observation only: kernel weights exp(-(y_obs - f)^2 / (2 x 0.005^2)) over all (sample, history, wait) states of the other samples.
policies.readiness_history: probe at the first decision time where the estimated success probability >= 0.9, using the known command history and all observations so far: sample weights proportional to exp(-sum (y_obs - f_j)^2 / (2 x 0.005^2)) over the other samples simulated under the same history.
policies.oracle: probe at the first wait at which the plant itself succeeds (lower bound; not implementable).

metrics: Readiness curves R(w | history): fraction of samples that succeed when probed at w.
Readiness among states whose noise-free reporter has returned to within 0.01 of baseline, by history.
Per policy and history: success rate, mean failure-penalized completion time, mean wait.
Matched reliability: for each adaptive policy, the shortest fixed wait whose success rate is at least as high, and its mean completion time.

statements.S1: Readiness of baseline-returned states differs between short and long histories.
statements.S2: readiness_history reaches its success rate with a shorter mean completion time than the fixed wait that matches that success rate.
statements.S3: readiness_history versus readiness_current: success rate and mean completion time.

reporting: All statements are reported whatever their outcome; no significance testing (deterministic simulation of one model).
